title: My new roommate labels everything he owns. This morning, my bedroom door had a label.
transcript:
My new roommate labels everything he owns. This morning, my bedroom door had a label. The label was on my bedroom door when I woke up. White tape, black marker, one word. His name.

Owen moved in two weeks ago. He's polite and quiet, and the day he arrived, he gave me a friendly slap on the back, right between the shoulders. Since then, he's been labeling things.

First his food. Then the couch. Then my coffee mug, the one my sister made me. Every label said Owen, in the same neat capitals.

I peeled the one off my door and knocked on his. No answer. But I could hear him in there, whispering. Practicing something. "Hey, it's me. Hey, it's me." In my voice.

So when he left for work, I went into his room. It was empty except for one cardboard box, taped shut. I cut it open.

It was full of old labels. Peeled off doors, mugs, cars. Each one had a different name crossed out, with Owen written underneath.

The last one in the box had my name on it. It wasn't crossed out yet.

Then I remembered that friendly slap, two weeks ago. I reached behind me, between my shoulders, and felt around.

My fingers found the edge of tape.
